summary.intent: Run a code quality review (reuse, quality, efficiency) on phase 35 TEE worker changes and fix any issues found.
summary.outcome: Three parallel review agents identified 6 actionable issues; all were fixed, TypeScript build passed clean, and all 56 tests passed. Changes committed.

repo: Phase 35 is the Phala Cloud TEE migration — 'testnet' in the directory name is a misnomer; Phala Cloud free tier runs on the same production Intel TDX nodes as paid deployments
tee-worker has distinct key helpers: getKeypair() (returns private+public) vs getPublicKey() (public only) — the public-key route was accidentally leaking the private key by calling the wrong one
Two competing env vars existed for the same concept: TEE_EPOCH and TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH — inconsistency across health and republish routes
The /republish endpoint lacked a batch size limit, creating an unbounded-work risk
Metrics middleware used req.path as a label on 404s, causing unbounded label cardinality in Prometheus

code.finding: Called getKeypair() instead of getPublicKey(), leaking the private key in the response — fixed to use getPublicKey()
Used TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH env var; harmonized with TEE_EPOCH used in republish route
Missing batch size cap on /republish; dead keyEpoch field in interface; redundant successes/failures counters — all fixed
404 handler used req.path as a Prometheus label — replaced with a static 'unknown' to prevent cardinality explosion

workflow: Getting a clean git diff for code review required multiple attempts with different diff strategies (two-dot, three-dot, merge-base) before finding a working approach

Launching all three review agents (reuse, quality, efficiency) in parallel then aggregating findings is an effective pattern — all three independently flagged the private key leak, confirming severity

Several findings were intentionally skipped as not worth the churn: probe deduplication, clearBytes vs fill(0), hexToBytes vs Buffer.from, sequential batch processing (deliberate security tradeoff), string zeroing JS limitation

friction: git diff retrieval required 8+ attempts with different flags and strategies before a working diff command was found — the repo/worktree setup made standard diff invocations fail silently or produce empty output
open_items: Probe deduplication: connection-test.ts and sdk-core share similar patterns — significant refactor deferred
clearBytes vs .fill(0) inconsistency — trivial cleanup deferred
hexToBytes vs Buffer.from inconsistency — trivial, Node-only context, deferred
Sequential batch processing in /republish could be parallelized but was left sequential as a deliberate security tradeoff
String zeroing in JS is fundamentally ineffective (GC/JIT can copy values) — a comment exists noting this limitation but no mitigation was added
